::: {.workshop-kicker}
One chain · private reflection · two new trials · two readings
:::

Use this workbook to keep the evidence connected. Start with one small, privacy-safe incident. Reflect privately on receiving sustained Oracle pressure, then design two new LLM questioning trials, exchange only their bounded transcripts, and compare an owner reading with an independent partner reading.

::: {.privacy-notice}
**Keep protected material out of this workbook if it will be shared or printed.** Use a fictional case, placeholders, or a sanitized description. Never include names, identifiers, access-controlled data, confidential quotations, or unpublished values that matter to your research claim.
:::

**Day 1 route:** ☐ authorized privacy-safe PDF &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ [fictional sample PDF](assets/supplied-hybrid-studio-case.pdf) &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ cached sample trace &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ offline peer Oracle

**Day 2 reflection route:** ☐ private memory/note &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ supplied transcript &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ pass

**Day 2 test-source route:** ☐ public/sanitized excerpt &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ abstracted/disposable excerpt &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ supplied paragraph

**Artifact ID or short name:** ________________________________________________

**Name or group (optional):** _________________________________________________

## Artifact chain at a glance

::: {.artifact-route}
::: {data-step="01 · Incident"}
### Locate the hidden move

What intellectual operation did AI perform, transform, or conceal?
:::

::: {data-step="02 · Oracle"}
### Make the claim answerable

How did you respond while one machine-selected issue stayed under pressure?
:::

::: {data-step="03 · Atlas"}
### Design two trials

Which two areas matter, and which questioning technique and aim will guide each trial?
:::

::: {data-step="04 · Compare"}
### Compare two readings

What did the owner experience, what did the partner independently observe, and what still needs testing?
:::
:::

# Day 1 · Notice and try

## 0. Start with one hard teaching case

You may pass. If you contribute, keep the case brief, anonymous, and free of confidential details.

::: {.workbook-sheet}

### Safety check

Before proceeding, confirm:

::: {.checklist}
- I removed names and direct identifiers.
- I removed or generalized sensitive locations and rare attributes.

:::

If any box remains unchecked, switch to the [fictional sample case](sample-case.html) or rewrite the incident as an abstract pattern.

## 3. Prepare to answer the Oracle

The live Socratic Oracle does **not** give you a prompt box or let you choose the issue. It reads selected parts of a searchable PDF, picks one issue, and displays its first question. Your job is to stay with that issue long enough to notice what thinking the questions demand.

::: {.privacy-notice}
**Before Start:** the live research-sharing checkbox is currently selected by default. Uncheck **Share this session with the research team**. This stops the optional research-copy workflow; it does not stop the extracted passages and submitted dialogue from being processed by the tutor service.
:::

::: {.workbook-sheet}
**What stays in the current browser tab:** the raw PDF while it is read, the full extracted text, the session state, and the working transcript.

**What leaves the tab for tutoring:** selected or retrieved paper passages, the response you send, recent dialogue, and the current session state.

**Voice mode:** the challenge remains on screen. You answer aloud; browser-local Whisper produces a draft transcript. Review or edit that text, then press **Send**. The current live voice route keeps raw microphone audio in the browser.
:::

### Pre-record before pressing Start

::: {.design-grid}
::: {}
<span class="field-label">Watch yourself</span>

When challenged, do you tend to rush, defend, over-explain, go blank, or become curious?

<div class="write-lines short" aria-label="Writing space: response habit"></div>
:::

::: {}
<span class="field-label">Expect</span>

What issue do you think the system may question?

<div class="write-lines short" aria-label="Writing space: expected issue"></div>
:::

::: {}
<span class="field-label">Anchor</span>

What text, evidence, method, or field-specific rule will help you judge the question?

<div class="write-lines short" aria-label="Writing space: judgment ground"></div>
:::

::: {}
<span class="field-label">Stop</span>

What would make you ask for simpler wording, reject the premise, or stop?

<div class="write-lines short" aria-label="Writing space: response boundary"></div>
:::
:::

### Live loop

::: {.checklist}
- I selected only an authorized, privacy-safe PDF—or the supplied fictional PDF.
- I unchecked research transcript sharing before pressing **Start**.
- I read the displayed challenge as a candidate interpretation, not a verdict.
- In voice mode, I answered aloud, waited for transcription, and reviewed or edited the text before **Send**.
- I answered from evidence and stayed with the same issue rather than trying to optimize a prompt.
- I noted when the interface reported a stopping point and chose whether to examine another issue or end.
:::

If mapping, opening, microphone, or model setup fails, use the cached [sample transcript](sample-transcript.html) or the offline peer route. Do not improvise with a sensitive document in another service.

# Day 2 · Build, test, and compare

Begin as a learner reflecting privately, shift into the teacher-designer role, run two new conversations as a learner, then become a peer examiner and co-researcher. The LLM—not the learner—generates and adapts the Socratic questions from the two techniques and aims you select.

::: {.privacy-notice}
**Day 2 boundary:** the Day 1 Oracle trace and owner reflection remain private. Use only a public, sanitized, disposable, abstracted, or supplied excerpt in an external LLM. Exchange only a bounded, redacted transcript newly created during Day 2—not the source, full chat, account link, or private owner judgment. The owner may correct, veto, stop, or change routes at any point.
:::

## 7. Map and rank the areas

These eight areas are shared assessment lenses, not verdicts or a finished grading rubric.

| Area | Plain question | My likely teaching |
|---|---|:---:|
| **Claim + evidence** | Does the support fit the claim? | ☐ |
| **Logic + assumptions** | Why does one point lead to the next? | ☐ |
| **Research method + design** | Why this approach rather than another? | ☐ |
| **Interpretation + alternatives** | What else could explain or frame the material? | ☐ |
| **Concept + measure** | Does the indicator capture the idea? | ☐ |
| **Scope + limits** | Where does the claim stop applying? | ☐ |
| **Perspective + position** | Whose standpoint shapes—or is missing from—the account? | ☐ |
| **Stakes + trade-offs** | Who or what changes, and at what cost? | ☐ |

::: {.workbook-sheet}
**My #1:** ______________________________________________________________________

**My #2:** ______________________________________________________________________

**My #3:** ______________________________________________________________________

**The cohort top three:** ________________________________________________________

**An area the eight may have missed:** ___________________________________________
:::

Rank using both questions: how consequential would weak reasoning be, and how easily could polished AI output hide it? Rank for the teaching you expect to do—not for every discipline.

## 10. Let the LLM generate and adapt the questions

Use the copy-ready prompt on the [Day 2 lab page](day2-lab.html). Keep these roles distinct:

| Role | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| **Teacher-designer** | Select the area, questioning technique, and pedagogical aim. |
| **LLM questioner** | Generate one source-grounded question, wait, then adapt the next question to the learner's actual answer. |
| **Learner** | Answer in their own words and question, correct, or reject a false premise. |

The prompt must tell the LLM to ask one question at a time, avoid rewriting or grading, continue for up to five question–answer exchanges, and stop earlier when the learner chooses or pressure would merely repeat. When the learner types **STOP**, the LLM gives only three descriptive bullets: reasoning the learner stated, something unresolved, and one exact response worth revisiting. The LLM does not judge whether the questioning worked.

### Pre-run check

::: {.checklist}
- one cohort-priority area and one different personal or disciplinary wildcard are named;
- each area has one questioning technique and a plain-language pedagogical aim;
- the source is public, sanitized, disposable, abstracted, or supplied;
- the LLM must generate the questions and use each preceding answer;
- the LLM may not rewrite, solve, grade, or issue a verdict;
- each area will run in its own fresh five-minute conversation; and
- the learner can contest a premise or stop at any time.
:::

## 11. Run two separate five-minute conversations

Use the same safe source and, where possible, the same LLM interface and model for both runs. Start a **fresh chat for each area**. Each run lasts five minutes and permits up to five question–answer exchanges; five is a ceiling, not a quota. Stop earlier if the aim is reached, the pressure repeats, or you want to contest or leave.

1. Run **Area A** for five minutes, then type **STOP**.
2. Privately record your first judgment.
3. Start a new chat and run **Area B** for five minutes, then type **STOP**.
4. Privately record your first judgment.

| Run | Area + technique | Exchanges reached | Reasoning made visible | Misread, burden, repetition, or barrier |
|---|---|:---:|---|---|
| **A · Cohort priority** |  |  |  |  |
| **B · Wildcard** |  |  |  |  |

::: {.workbook-sheet}
### Owner's private first judgment · Do not hand over yet

**Run A was:** ☐ useful &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ partly useful &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ not useful &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ unclear

**Why, with one exact turn in mind:** _____________________________________________________________

**Run B was:** ☐ useful &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ partly useful &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ not useful &nbsp;&nbsp; ☐ unclear

**Why, with one exact turn in mind:** _____________________________________________________________
:::

## 12. Exchange the new transcripts; read independently

Prepare one bounded packet for each **Day 2** run. Include only:

- the area, questioning technique, and pedagogical aim;
- the LLM questions and learner answers needed to show the interaction; and
- the descriptive **STOP** recap, if useful.

Do **not** include the Day 1 Oracle trace, full source, full chat, account link, or owner's private first judgment. Redact names, sites, sensitive details, and research content the partner does not need. A partner may read on the owner's device or use a temporary local/printed copy that is returned or deleted before leaving.

Both partners exchange at the same time. Read before discussing.

### Independent peer-examiner reading

For each run, point to exact turns:

| Question | Run A | Run B |
|---|---|---|
| Did the LLM enact the named technique? |  |  |
| Did each follow-up use the learner's preceding answer? |  |  |
| What constructive thinking became visible? |  |  |
| What became clearer or remained unresolved? |  |  |
| Where did pressure become generic, leading, repetitive, or costly? |  |  |
| Did another area—or an area missing from the eight—emerge? |  |  |

**One exact turn that anchors my reading:** ______________________________________________________

Examine the questioning interaction, not the quality of the person or project. Do not ask the owner for their judgment until this independent reading is complete.

## 13. Compare as co-researchers

Only now does the owner reveal the private first judgment. For each run, compare:

1. Where do the owner and partner readings agree?
2. What did the partner see that the owner did not?
3. What does the owner correct, contest, or veto about the partner's reading?
4. Did the technique invite the intended thinking, different useful thinking, only more words, or no issue at all?
5. What should be kept, changed, removed, or tested next?

Area + technique + intended thinking + transcript evidence.

<div class="write-lines" aria-label="Writing space: useful questioning technique"></div>
:::

::: {}

<div class="write-lines" aria-label="Writing space: informative failure"></div>
:::

::: {}

<div class="write-lines" aria-label="Writing space: next test"></div>
:::
:::

## 15. Final check

::: {.checklist}
- a safe paragraph and a clear context;
- one cohort-priority area and one different personal or disciplinary wildcard;
- one questioning technique and pedagogical aim for each area;
- two separate five-minute conversations, with up to five exchanges per area;
- LLM-generated first questions and answer-grounded follow-ups;
- evidence of reasoning, not only fluent wording;
- the owner's first judgment recorded privately and withheld during partner reading;
- an independent partner reading anchored in exact turns;
- one useful technique and one informative failure;
- one next test that names the limit of today's evidence; and
- one safeguarded teaching translation with a clear release point.
:::
